name: Two-phase immersion tank
summary: Servers sit in a fluorocarbon bath that boils on the chips and condenses on a water coil in the lid. Very high density, but the fluids are PFAS and 3M stopped making Novec and Fluorinert at the end of 2025, so new projects have stalled.

maxRackW.note: LiquidStack markets its 48U DataTank at up to 252 kW (vendor listing seen in search, not opened).

toTechnicalLoop.note: Vapor condenses on the in-tank coil; small losses through the lid and when the tank is opened.

min.note: Condenser water must stay well below the fluid's boiling point (49 °C for Novec 649).

max.note: Above ~40 °C the condenser cannot hold vapor pressure with a 49 to 61 °C boiling fluid.

deltaTK.note: Condenser water rise; the bath itself is isothermal at the boiling point.

pressureDropKpa.note: Condenser coil water-side drop, similar to single-phase tank CDUs.

addedWeightKgPerRack.note: Fluorocarbons are ~1.6 kg/L (Novec 649), about double a hydrocarbon oil, so a filled tank outweighs a single-phase tank.

tankFootprintM2PerRack.note: 48U tank; no published footprint found. Assumed slightly larger than a 39 OU single-phase tank (2.22 m²).

pumpPowerFraction.note: No fluid pump in the bath (passive boiling); condenser water pump only.

capexUsdPerKw.note: Sealed tank plus fluorocarbon fill at several times hydrocarbon-oil prices per litre, and fluid now scarce.

installWeeks.note: Sealed tanks, vapor management and fluid handling.

leadTimeWeeks.note: Fluid supply is the constraint after 3M's PFAS exit; replacements (e.g. Chemours Opteon 2P50) are not yet at scale.
